title: Make internal/testutil/headless take the browser from CHROME_BIN only (refusing Edge) and skip with a message naming CHROME_BIN otherwise
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: C1 (from HOW 1): with CHROME_BIN set to an existing browser executable, the helper returns and starts exactly that file: missing
C2 (from HOW 2 and WHY): with CHROME_BIN unset, the calling test is skipped (testing's Skip) with a message naming CHROME_BIN, even with Chrome or Edge installed in a standard place: missing
C3 (from HOW 3): with CHROME_BIN set to a path that is not an existing file, the test is skipped with a message: missing
C4 (from HOW 4 and WHAT): with HBAND_TEST_BROWSER set and CHROME_BIN unset, the test still skips: no fallback to any other variable or browser: missing
C5 (from title and HOW 5): Edge is never started, even when installed, and the helper refuses Edge: partial
C6 (from HOW 6 and WHAT): the helper's source holds no hard-coded browser install path and no read of any browser-path variable other than CHROME_BIN: missing
C7 (from HOW 7): default_browser_test.go and edge_default_test.go assert the CHROME_BIN-only rule, and `go test -count=1 ./...` passes with CHROME_BIN unset on a machine with no browser: missing

C8 (from WHAT): search the whole repository (scripts, docs, CI) for other places that pick a browser path, report them, fix the ones that are the same defect, and name the ones that are a different kind of change: missing
README.md:82-87 and :108 still describe HBAND_TEST_BROWSER and the two Program Files paths. That is documentation, which is outside slice work; the code is what is true.

tests/acceptance/run_finish.py (BROWSER_PATH regex at :70, edge_risk at :105-121), check_run_finish_needs_chrome_bin.py and test_run_finish_edge_guard.py are a different kind of change: a guard on browser paths inside ledger finish bodies, not a browser picker for Go tests. SC-043 deletes them, so I left them alone.

The approved ledger finish body for E-004 line 2 (test_e004_2, Q-028) hard-codes an msedge fallback and ignores CHROME_BIN. It lives only in the ledger, not in the tree, and no slice code can change it. .taad/slices/SL-008/run_finish_e004_2.py already follows the CHROME_BIN-only rule.

The project's recorded testing stack still says 'otherwise the default Edge path is used' and names HBAND_TEST_BROWSER as a test setting. Both are now untrue: the browser comes from CHROME_BIN only, and CHROME_BIN is not an HBAND_TEST_* name. The record needs the edit; it is not in this repository, so I could not make it.

Repository search for other browser pickers (C8): Go has exactly one, headless.go, fixed here; its only caller is internal/server/browser_test.go:151, which needed no change. No CI files or shell scripts are tracked. The only other hits are README.md (stale docs), the three Python files under tests/acceptance (SC-043) and the SL-008 scratch runner, which already conforms.
The README's browser-test paragraph needs correcting outside slice work, since it now describes the old variables.

deviation: No settings checkbox or on-screen notice was built for the Edge refusal or the CHROME_BIN-only rule. The standing workaround rule is written for an app with settings. This is a test-only helper with no settings or UI, and the owner's rule (restated by the engine for this machine) is that Edge is never started. A switch to turn the refusal off would contradict it. Edge's first-run behaviour (signing the profile in to the Windows Microsoft account and importing old browsing history) is an outside defect, and the skip message states it in plain words next to the skipped result.

deviation: Edge refusal matches a lower-cased base name containing 'msedge' or 'microsoft-edge', wider than the design's literal msedge.exe, so msedge without .exe, MSEDGE.EXE and the Linux package name are refused too. The check runs before the file lookup, so a missing Edge path is also refused by name.
